4. At the trial the plaintiff examined 5 witness and proved Exhibit-1, C. S. Khatian, Exhibit-2 'Dhol forth' Ext. 3-3(5) dakhilas and Ext. 4, an extract from pattani register, calling for the original in proof of her case. But she did not depose herself. The defendants produced 3 witnesses for each set and proved documents, Exhibit Ka and Kha in support of the defence. 

 9. Leave was granted to consider the appellants submissions, first, that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in shifting the onus on the defendants and presuming that since the pattani book was produced from the custody of the defendant-Government and since the defendants issued certified copy thereof the plaintiff respondent succeeded in proving her settlement of the suit land from the ex-landlord, secondly that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the suit was not barred by limitation inasmuch as the suit was not filed within six years from the date of publication of the impugned S. A. Khatian as required under Article 120 of the first schedule to the Limitation Act, and lastly that the learned Judges of the High Court Division erred in law in interfering with the finding of facts arrived at by the lower appellate court on consideration of the evidence on record. 

 17. Incidentally, it may be mentioned that the question of limitation with regard to the prayer respecting the S.A. Khatian though raised is only an ancillary question and has no effect on the main relief sought. This question has lost its significance in view of the failure of the suit as a whole.
